_provenance: SOURCE-DERIVED, NOT LIVE (prompt-user rules only load from system /etc/codex/requirements.toml or cloud/MDM requirements; not settable in a throwaway CODEX_HOME). Built from codex-rs @ rust-v0.167.0: core/src/tools/approvals.rs request_approval_with_user_prompt, core/src/tools/sandboxing.rs ExecApprovalRequirement::NeedsHumanApproval, app-server README 'prompt-user', schema CommandExecutionApprovalKind, test core/tests/suite/scenarios_managed_human_approval_tests.rs. Angle-bracket values are placeholders.
requirements_toml_example:
[[rules.prefix_rules]]
pattern = [{ token = "echo" }]
decision = "prompt-user"
justification = "A person must approve this command."
_hook_notes: Byte-for-byte the same shape as an ordinary command approval: no field marks it as a prompt-user checkpoint. The hook IS invoked. A hook {behavior:'deny'} wins. A hook {behavior:'allow'} is IGNORED (match arm `Some(Allow) if !ctx.requires_human_approval()`), and Codex then asks a person anyway (terminal / capable app-server client).

messages._note: Only sent to clients that initialized with capabilities {experimentalApi:true, requiredHumanApproval:true}. Valid replies: accept | decline | cancel. With no capable client connected the command is rejected.
